object.description: The whole stack as it stood on the pad: the orbiter riding a tank of liquid hydrogen and oxygen the size of a grain silo, with two solid boosters strapped alongside that burned for two minutes and came down by parachute to be used again. Two million kilograms at lift-off, seven million pounds of thrust, and the first spacecraft to fly to orbit and land on a runway, 135 times from 1981 to 2011. It built the space station, carried Hubble up and fixed it five times, and lost two crews, Challenger in 1986 and Columbia in 2003. It stands here at its full 56 metres, off to the east; the orbiter Discovery, the real one, stands on the lane a little further on.
facts: The external tank was the only part thrown away each flight; it was painted white twice, then left orange to save 270 kg.
The main engines burned hydrogen at 3,300 degrees inside chambers cooled by the same hydrogen flowing through their walls.
Five orbiters flew: Columbia, Challenger, Discovery, Atlantis and Endeavour; Enterprise flew only glide tests.
The programme cost about 200 billion dollars; a launch cost around 450 million.
